review_rubric.requirement: Verify at least 15 accepted, topic-matched primary papers and read their full text before finalizing the experiment and visual plans.
review_rubric.failure: Preprints, workshops or title-only search results are counted as accepted main-conference peers.

review_rubric.requirement: Bind every principal claim to executed measurements and an experiment with a clear argumentative duty.
review_rubric.failure: A planner prediction, model-written number, synthetic replacement, or passing self-authored test is presented as an observed result.

review_rubric.requirement: Evaluate full relevant test splits or a justified prespecified sample with uncertainty; compare scale to the closest peers and expand evidence where generality claims require it.
review_rubric.failure: A few convenient examples or a tiny plotted sample substitutes for the primary evaluation.

review_rubric.requirement: Include the strongest relevant competing methods and simple diagnostic baselines under comparable data, model, budget and evaluator conditions.
review_rubric.failure: Only weak baselines or unmarked copied scores support the central advantage.

review_rubric.requirement: Remove each claimed mechanism, test meaningful operating conditions, and resolve alternative explanations.
review_rubric.failure: An architecture diagram is treated as proof of the mechanism, or inconvenient observations are omitted from the scientific record.

review_rubric.requirement: Use independent repetitions where stochastic variation affects conclusions; report denominators, dispersion or confidence intervals and paired comparisons where applicable.
review_rubric.failure: Repeated adaptive retries are called independent seeds or best-of-k results are compared with pass-at-one without labeling.

review_rubric.requirement: Choose diagrams, plots and tables according to their explanatory duty and data structure; analytical charts must be produced from observed data.
review_rubric.failure: Decorative generated images impersonate measurements, or several isolated points are expanded into redundant charts.

review_rubric.requirement: Default architecture figures explain a grounded problem bottleneck, the specific mechanism or information-flow intervention, and an evidence-supported consequence or visibly labeled testable expectation. Explicit simple-method requests retain their supplied topology without fabricated scientific claims.
evidence_required: specific intervention and labeled information dependencies
actual input, output and operating boundary
measured consequence binding or explicit hypothesis and discriminating test
baseline identity and neutral structure or actual limitation evidence
candidate-specific scientific, visual and editorial reviews at final print size
review_rubric.failure: A generic module directory passes as an explanatory scientific architecture, a causal arrow is claimed as empirical proof, or a baseline failure/winning outcome is invented to improve the picture.

review_rubric.requirement: Place the overview beside the introduced method or problem; place each result visual next to its first substantive discussion and cite it in the text.
review_rubric.failure: Visuals collect at the manuscript end, move before their premise, or captions and references become detached.

review_rubric.requirement: Have separate reviewers inspect scientific fidelity, quantitative analysis, comparative information value, and rendered layout before selecting final candidates.
review_rubric.failure: The image generator self-approves without a data or layout audit.

review_rubric.requirement: Repeat benchmark comparison, experiment repair, manuscript revision and rendered review until concrete acceptance criteria pass or the authorized resource budget is exhausted.
review_rubric.failure: A time, money or infrastructure stop is silently reported as meeting the scientific delivery requirements.

comparison_summary.interpretation: Descriptive context only. Count matching is not a gate or proof of scientific quality.
